item.title: Pesach Sameach from the World Jewish Congress - World Jewish Congress
item.description: Passover, the Festival of Spring, is a time of renewal - an opportunity to look to the future, take stock of priorities, and rid ourselves of any “chametz,” or spiritual clutter, making space for growth both as individuals and as communities. At the WJC we have taken this to heart and have sharpened our organizational focus on our core mission to advocate for the wellbeing of our affiliated communities globally and to combat antisemitism in all its manifestations.

item.title: World Jewish Congress Report Finds Systemic Bias and Terrorist Propaganda on Arabic-Language Wikipedia - World Jewish Congress
item.description: A report published by WJC’s Technology and Human Rights Institute found that Arabic-language Wikipedia articles perpetuate anti-Israel bias and terror propaganda. Finding that more than 25% of citations in key articles originated from Hamas, Hezbollah, or other terrorist propaganda platforms, the WJC called on the Wikimedia Foundation to take urgent action to restore neutrality and accountability on Arabic Wikipedia.

item.title: World Jewish Congress Sends Letter of Condolence to Bahrain and UAE Amid Ongoing Iranian Strikes - World Jewish Congress
item.description: The World Jewish Congress extended its condolences to the leaders of Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates on Monday, expressing solidarity with both nations as they continue to face Iranian missile and drone attacks that have killed and wounded civilians across the Gulf. The letters addressed respectively to King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa of Bahrain and President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan of the UAE, come as the conflict enters the third full week.

item.title: WJC Executive Vice President Maram Stern | It Can Happen Anywhere - World Jewish Congress
item.description: In an editorial by WJC Executive Vice President Maram Stern, he warns that the rise of global antisemitism calls for increased security and governmental support now more than ever.

item.title: WJC Leads Discussion on Faith, Feminism, and Online Hate at UN Commission on the Status of Women - World Jewish Congress
item.description: In partnership with more than a dozen UN Permanent Missions and civil society organizations, the WJC on Thursday hosted a high-level parallel virtual event on the sidelines of the UN’s 70th Commission on the Status of Women (CSW) in New York. The event examined how conspiracy theories and online disinformation contribute to gender-based violence against women and undermine their role in the ongoing effort to safeguard universal human rights.
